reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Craniotomy for a frontal glioma with signs of rising ICP overnight (headache, vomiting, drowsier, BP up, HR down, shift 6 to 8 mm), apixaban taken yesterday against plan with anti-Xa 62, a missed levetiracetam dose, and untreated steroid hyperglycemia with falling sodium.

asa.rationale: Intracranial mass with worsening mass effect and clinical deterioration.

decision.recommendation: urgent: escalate now, reverse, then proceed
decision.rationale: The neurologic decline needs the neurosurgery attending now; surgery likely becomes more urgent, not less. Measurable apixaban before a craniotomy needs reversal per protocol (andexanet or 4 factor PCC). Load levetiracetam, start insulin, treat ICP.

redFlags.evidence: Worse headache, vomiting x2, harder to wake (GCS 14), BP 164/96 with HR 56; CT midline shift 8 mm (was 6), ventricle effacement; resident notified, no action.
redFlags.implication: Herniation risk; anesthetic choices affect ICP.
redFlags.action: Escalate to attending; head up, avoid hypercarbia and hypoxia, mannitol or hypertonic saline, no sedating premedication, smooth induction.

redFlags.finding: Apixaban taken 23 h ago with measurable level
redFlags.evidence: Pharmacy med rec: resumed at home, last 10/26 0800; anti-Xa apixaban 62 ng/mL; H&P assumed last dose 10/23.
redFlags.action: Neurosurgery and hematology decision: reversal (andexanet alfa or 4 factor PCC per protocol) or delay.

redFlags.evidence: Levetiracetam 2000 dose held because of an NPO order without a meds clause.
redFlags.action: Give IV levetiracetam now; fix the NPO order.

redFlags.evidence: Glucose 231 to 251 on dexamethasone; no insulin ordered.
redFlags.implication: Hyperglycemia worsens neurologic outcomes and infection risk.
redFlags.action: Insulin infusion with a 140 to 180 target.

redFlags.finding: Falling sodium with low serum osmolality
redFlags.evidence: Na 133 to 131, serum osm 272, urine osm 410, urine Na 62.
redFlags.implication: Hyponatremia worsens cerebral edema (SIADH or cerebral salt wasting).
redFlags.action: Isotonic or hypertonic fluids only, trend sodium.

redFlags.evidence: SSEP and tcMEP; TIVA requested, no relaxant after intubation; bite blocks.
redFlags.action: Propofol and remifentanil TIVA, no paralysis after intubation, bite blocks.

planItems.item: TIVA with propofol and remifentanil; mannitol standby
Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min of incision
Levetiracetam 1000 mg IV, normocarbia, head up

boothComplications.why: Airway instrumentation in a pinned head
